page.layout: One page of verse, one column, centred; a large woodcut-style initial Q and C at the left of two poems; a fleuron ornament below the text. Faint show-through from the reverse page in the right half and right margin (not transcribed). Stamps and shelf mark at the foot (not transcribed).

main_text.l: N. R.
QVa putris intortis fundit se in brachia nodis
Arbor, in infames noxa parata reos:
Hîc regna: hîc arces: hîc nostri portus Amoris:
Hîc vitæ fulcrum deliciumq; meæ.
Hîc lethi spolium, partiq; insigne trophæi
Christe tui: hîc sonti est ara parata gregi.
Quæ pietas! hostes in partiiura triumphi,
In partes regni Christe vocare tui!
O flamma, ô amor, ô æterni fomes Amoris!
Vitam è vulneribus vulneris autor habet.
Fronde carens arbor pleno se germine prodit,
Et radice carens vertice summa ferit.
Quamq; notat præceps infami nomine vulgus,
Hinc vitæ & famæ manat origo meæ.
Nulla alia hos fructus, nulla hos tulit arbor Amores, Nec Libani tales procreat hortus opes.
Et mortem dubitet quis pro crucis arce pacisci,
In media noster si cruce regnat Amor?
I. M.
CHriste tuo partos ne despice sanguine vernas,
Qui vitæ hac ponunt in trabe fulcra suæ. Excute vitalem gelidis præcordibus ignem,
Queis posita in Flamma est spes, salusq; tua.
Nam quid? ad hunc si Christe tuum torpebimus
ignem, Quis miseris poterit iam satis esse calor?
CRVX TVA NOSTER AMOR: quid non speremus
Aman- Fortius in media si cruce feruet amor. (res?

page.notes: Printed "(res?" at the right end of the last line appears to be a catchword-like mark or a reference, read tentatively. Marginal words "Amores"/"Amor" in the right half belong to show-through and are omitted. The woodcut fleuron below the text is an ornament, not transcribed. Several words in the verse are uncertain due to scan quality, e.g. "partiiura" (possibly "partiturae"), "(res?" and the final word of the Christe poem line 1 hyphenated "Aman-" / "Fortius".
